simple: A `ModuleScript` is a script that holds code you want to use in many places. Instead of copying the same function into ten scripts, you write it once in a module and load it with `require`. Modules in ReplicatedStorage can even be shared by the server and players' devices. This page shows how to build modules and some smart ways to use them.
analogy: A ModuleScript is like a shared toolbox in a classroom: instead of every student bringing their own hammer, everyone borrows the same one from the box whenever they need it.
keyPoints: Every ModuleScript starts as `local module = {}` and `return module`. Whatever it returns is what other scripts get.
A module can return anything except `nil`, but usually returns a table full of functions or data.
Load a module with `require(...)`. Use `WaitForChild` on the client so you do not try to load it before it has arrived.
A module only runs once per side. Every later `require` gets the exact same table, so changes to it are shared.
The server and the client each get their own separate copy of the module's result.
Two modules that `require` each other cause a 'required recursively' error. Avoid circles.
Common uses: storing settings data (like gun stats), creating custom events, and wrapping messy code (like networking) behind simple functions.

terms.ModuleScript: A script that does not run by itself. It runs when another script `require`s it, and gives back a value.
terms.require: A function that loads a ModuleScript and returns what it returns.
terms.return value: The thing a module hands back, such as a table of functions.
terms.reference: A pointer to the same thing, not a copy. If two scripts hold a reference to one table and one changes it, both see the change.
terms.client-server boundary: The line between the server and players' devices. Each side runs its own copy of code.
terms.circular require: When module A requires module B and B requires A. Roblox stops this with an error.
terms.WaitForChild: Waits until a child with that name exists, then returns it. Useful because things might not be loaded yet.
terms.BindableEvent: An object that lets scripts on the same side send signals to each other.
terms.encapsulation: Hiding complicated details inside a module and giving other scripts a simple function to call instead.
terms.configuration data: Settings like `MagazineSize = 20` or `Damage = 50` that many scripts need to read.

example.title: Share a pickup bonus calculator
example.place: ModuleScript named PickupManager in ReplicatedStorage, plus a Script in ServerScriptService
example.code:
-- ModuleScript named "PickupManager" in ReplicatedStorage
local PickupManager = {}

local defaultMultiplier = 1.25
local rarityMultipliers = {
	common = 10,
	uncommon = 20,
	rare = 50,
	legendary = 100,
}

function PickupManager.getPickupBonus(rarity)
	return rarityMultipliers[rarity] * defaultMultiplier
end

return PickupManager

--[[ Script in ServerScriptService (separate script):
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local PickupManager = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("PickupManager"))

print(PickupManager.getPickupBonus("legendary")) --> 125
]]
explain: The module makes a table called `PickupManager`.
It stores how much each rarity is worth, like `legendary = 100`.
`getPickupBonus` looks up the rarity and multiplies it by 1.25, so legendary gives 100 x 1.25 = 125.
The module returns the table so other scripts can use it.
Any script (server or client) can `require` it and call `PickupManager.getPickupBonus`.

watchOut: Forgetting `return` at the end of a module causes an error when you require it.
Modules run only once. Do not expect code at the top of a module to run again each time you require it.
Do not make two modules require each other. Move the shared part into a third module.
Modules in ServerScriptService or ServerStorage cannot be required by the client. Use ReplicatedStorage for shared code.
